machine: Apple M1 Max, 32 GB unified memory

case.prompt: A red fox asleep beside a mossy stone in soft morning light.

method.execution: One C+ command performs native tokenization, the text-only Qwen3-VL encoder, dynamic prompt-sized metadata and RoPE, PyTorch-compatible seeded noise, the cached 40-step transformer trajectory, VAE decode, RGBA conversion, and PNG output.
method.memory_phases: The 17.5 GB text checkpoint mappings are released before the 12.42 GiB packed transformer is opened; transformer resources are released before the 1.35 GB VAE is opened.
method.noise: PyTorch 2.9 CPU MT19937 and scalar 16-value Box-Muller path, followed by ties-to-even BF16 conversion.
method.rope: Exact QwenImage21Rope three-axis position construction for a prompt prefix followed by a centered 16x16 target grid.

arbitrary_prompt_smoke.prompt: A blue ceramic teapot on a windowsill.
arbitrary_prompt_smoke.timing_note: Recorded before the transformer 32x32 output-tile optimization; retained as the variable-length functional smoke result.

reasoning.separate_integrated_limits: The fixture-fed trajectory retains its 1.1% final-latent and 1.3% decoded-FP32 gates. The native text encoder is independently bounded at 4% against the Torch 2.9 text fixture, whose result also differs by 3.28% from a Torch 2.8 MPS regeneration. Its small embedding drift measures 1.75609% after 40 denoising steps and 1.69086% after decode, so the integrated native-prompt boundaries use a measured 2% budget without weakening the fixture-fed tests.
reasoning.final_image: The canonical generated image remains within 0.957296% normalized RMS in RGBA byte space, with a 0.5574 mean absolute byte error. This is the downstream prompt-equivalence gate rather than an assertion that the text encoder is bit-identical across PyTorch backends.
reasoning.transformer_optimization: A 16x16 threadgroup now computes a 32x32 output tile with four accumulators per thread while retaining a 16-wide K tile and the original inner accumulation order. Transformer GPU time fell from 148823 ms to 98843.8 ms (33.6%) with every numerical metric unchanged.

limitations: Generation is currently fixed to 256x256, batch size one, text-to-image, and 40 denoising steps.
Prompts are limited to 498 post-template tokens because the text encoder currently accepts at most 512 full-template tokens.
Only the canonical prompt has a pinned end-to-end image oracle; arbitrary prompts are checked for finite execution but cannot be numerically compared without a matching reference fixture.
The optimized transformer still takes roughly 99 seconds of summed GPU kernel time at 256px and is not interactive.
Text weights remain original BF16 and require a separate 17.5 GB residency phase; text quantization, command-buffer batching, and further kernel optimization remain future work.
